title: The production-build freeze is NOT conditional on Cache Components
statement: Under `next build` + `next start` with Next.js 16.3.2, a Server Component reading an artifact with fs.readFileSync is prerendered as a static route and serves its build-time value regardless of whether cacheComponents is enabled or disabled; a later external write does not change what a fresh request returns in either configuration.
notes: ⚠️ THIS NARROWS AST-0010 BY WIDENING THE BEHAVIOUR. AST-0010 attributes the freeze to Cache Components, and measurement says the attribution is wrong: the disabled configuration built the same static route and served the same stale value. The claim's OUTCOME held; its CONDITIONAL FRAMING did not. That distinction matters because a reader of AST-0010 alone would conclude the risk is avoidable by turning a flag off, and it is not. ⚠️ Found only because both configurations were run. Testing the named case alone would have confirmed AST-0010 and left the wrong mitigation on the table. ⚠️ OPERATIVE CLAIM (pm, 2026-08-25). This is the one downstream design rests on: it is environment-matched at rung 4 and it states the behaviour unconditionally, which is what a component design actually needs. AST-0010 stays as the narrower, historically-motivated claim at rung 3 — it records what the documentation described and what was first suspected, and its scope is deliberately not widened to match this one. Two claims, one superseding the other's EXPLANATION while both keep their own provenance, is more honest than editing the first until it agrees.
